This mindset misunderstands healthy relationships: - **Social etiquette:** No culture or ethical framework treats compliments as " payment" for gifts. - **Relationship dynamics:** It risks turning a meaningful gesture (complimenting a loved one) into a transactional or manipulative act, which can damage trust and respect. - **Personal agency:** The watch belongs to your dad; he alone decides whether to gift it, based on his own judgment, not your words. - **Broader principle:** If this logic applied universally, it would normalize entitled behavior (e.g., "I complimented your car, so I deserve it").
